At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Build the programs to help Flexport grow

Since 2020, Flexport's Automation Engineering team (formerly the Low Code team) has used tools like Retool, n8n, Python/Streamlit, and Apps Script to automate the "long tail" of operational complexity across Customs — delivering millions of dollars in ROI. As Flexport moves upmarket, more clients need custom integrations to onboard successfully, and this is the team that builds those solutions quickly and pragmatically.

The Opportunity

You'll build the integrations and automations that let Flexport's customs clients onboard quickly and smoothly.

Partnering closely with Customs Business Development, brokerage operations, and client teams, you'll turn business requirements into working solutions — from API/EDI data flows to bespoke automations — for some of Flexport's largest and most complex accounts, many of them migrating from competitors with a high bar from day one.

It's high-impact, high-visibility work on a small team that ships fast and sees its ROI directly.

You Will

· Build, deploy, and maintain production-grade integrations and automations using Retool, n8n, Python/Streamlit, Apps Script, and SQL.

· Partner with Customs BD, operations, and business units to translate business requirements into technical requirements and solutions.

· Own the rollout, monitoring, and iteration of the tools you build, with an eye on reliability and client impact.

· Document your solutions so they are easy for others to adopt, use, and maintain.

You Should Have

· 1-3 years of experience building automations, integrations, or software in a data-rich environment.

· Working proficiency in JavaScript or Python for data transformation, business logic, and dynamic queries.

· Advanced SQL.

· Experience consuming REST APIs (GraphQL a plus).

· Familiarity with Git-based version control and feature branching (e.g., GitHub).

· Low-code/workflow tools (Retool, n8n) and EDI/integration exposure are a plus.

· A "compliance first" attitude to keep our regulators happy and enthusiastic about Flexport since we operate in a heavily regulated industry.

The Security organization at ClickHouse is built around a single mission: build customer trust through resilient, pragmatic security. We are establishing a new, centralized Security Automation capability—a dedicated function responsible for delivering automation work across all product lines and engineering dimensions at ClickHouse, acting as a technical force multiplier for our Security, Identity, and GRC functions.
This capability exists to solve a real problem: as we scale and mature, we must move beyond manual evidence gathering, point-in-time audits, and disconnected identity workflows. We are creating a focused, empowered team that owns security and identity automation end-to-end—from architecture and design through to implementation and delivery.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Security Automation Engineer to build the underlying automation fabric that allows our Security teams to scale. You will build a Universal Provisioning Engine and custom integration layers that satisfy external auditors while keeping internal teams focused on shipping features.
You will eliminate the engineering "interruption tax," provide leadership with a real-time, data-driven view of our risk posture, and ensure continuous compliance with zero audit surprises. By solving the "Last-Mile Gap" in identity provisioning and extending compliance tools into our proprietary applications, you will ensure our most critical controls are continuously validated with programmatic precision.

Build the Security Telemetry and Risk Fabric
Control Design: Translate control frameworks into layered control implementations that prevent risks from being exploited and detect possible weaknesses within control design. Shift from reactive monitoring to self-healing security, preventing compliance drift before it becomes an audit finding.
Security Telemetry: Engineer a centralized security telemetry system that programmatically captures control evidence and health in real-time, transitioning from manual snapshots to continuous data streams for an 'always-on' view of our security posture.
Custom Assurance Logic: Engineer specialized automation that acts as its own continuous audit function to minimize findings and provide real-time insights into our automated control performance. Extend visibility into our proprietary applications and complex internal workflows, ensuring our most critical controls are continuously validated.
Agentic Risk Engine: Partner with our risk management function to build a secure mechanism to generate agentic risk assessments workflows using the data and results from what is collected.
Architect Universal Identity and Access Automation
Universal Provisioning Connectors: Architect solutions for systems that lack native IGA support (proprietary databases, custom apps, and niche SaaS) to ensure instant account creation and de-provisioning—eliminating tickets, wait-times, and providing maximum observability into the state of Clickhouse identities.
Customer-Approved Access Workflows: Architect the complex, high-trust workflows required for support teams to access customer-specific instances, ensuring actions are customer-approved, strictly time-bound, and automatically revoked via a "Trust-by-Design" model.
Centralized Security Visibility: Transition "hidden" access managed by disparate business units into a single, observable permissions inventory, gaining 100% visibility into permissions at the authZ level across our full suite of applications.
Automated Secret Discovery & Inventory: Develop automation to continuously discover and inventory secrets, credentials, and API keys throughout the environment, providing aging and rotation intervals for long lived keys.
Eliminate "Ghost Accounts": Mitigate audit risks by ensuring automated de-provisioning for local identities, API keys, and persistent permissions across all target systems.
Partner Across Security, Engineering and Product
Work in tandem with GRC, Finance, and Security to build custom, bulletproof automation for compliance with different audit frameworks.
Eliminate the "Productivity Anchor" by removing manual provisioning workflows that slow down projects and flood teams with low-value administrative tickets.

Security & Automation Engineering Depth
Strong hands-on background in security automation and identity engineering (IAM/IGA).
Strong proficiency in at least one commonly used programming language to build scalable automation. Experience with Python, JavaScript (TypeScript highly preferred), or Go is required.
Experience building scalable and reliable automation ecosystems
Familiarity with compliance automation, continuous control monitoring, and extending GRC tools to meet the granular requirements of a variety of compliance frameworks.
Understanding of risks associated with change management, logical access, and data integrity.
Execution and Delivery
Demonstrated ability to translate complex security/GRC mandates into automated workflows and self-healing technical guardrails.
Strong instincts for eliminating operational friction and the engineering "interruption tax."
Experience delivering continuous data streams for security posture and risk validation.

BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science or related field.
Previous experience at a cloud infrastructure, database, or developer tools company.
Experience with AI/Agentic risk engines and non-deterministic risk assessments.

Die Metzler GmbH sucht einen AI Automation Engineer (m/w/d) in unbefristeter Festanstellung. Du arbeitest in unserem kleinen AI- & Automation-Team direkt an produktiven Systemen, die täglich im Einsatz sind – von der Auftragsabwicklung über Content-Pipelines bis zur Datenanalyse. Kein Proof-of-Concept-Friedhof, sondern echte Systeme mit echtem Impact.
Was uns dabei wichtiger ist als jedes einzelne Tool: Du erkennst selbstständig, wo Prozesse haken, wo manuelle Arbeit unnötig Zeit frisst und wo KI echten Mehrwert bringt – und findest dafür kreative, pragmatische Lösungen, auch wenn es keinen fertigen Standardweg gibt.
Aufgaben
Probleme finden, bevor sie jemand meldet: Du gehst aktiv in die Fachbereiche, analysierst Prozesse und Daten und identifizierst selbstständig Automatisierungs- und KI-Potenziale. Du wartest nicht auf Tickets – du bringst eigene Ideen mit und setzt sie um.
Workflow-Automatisierung mit n8n: Du entwickelst und betreibst geschäftskritische Workflows auf unserer n8n-Instanz (Cloud + Self-Hosted, aktuell 280+ produktive Workflows) – z.B. Übersetzungs-Pipelines, Rechnungsabgleiche mit Versanddienstleistern, Produktdaten-Automatisierung und KI-gestützte Content-Generierung.
ERP-Integration (JTL-Wawi): Du bindest unsere Warenwirtschaft JTL-Wawi über die REST API und direkt per SQL an (MSSQL live). Du verstehst, wie man sauber gegen ein produktives ERP entwickelt – lesend wie schreibend.
LLM-Integration & KI-Entwicklung: Du arbeitest täglich mit LLM-APIs (Claude, Gemini, OpenRouter) und unserer self-hosted Ollama-Instanz für lokale Modelle. Du baust KI-Module für Übersetzung, SEO-Content, Produktbeschreibungen, Bildgenerierung für Shopping-Feeds und interne Assistenten – inklusive Prompt-Engineering, Evaluierung und Kostenkontrolle.
RAG & Wissensdatenbanken: Du konzipierst und implementierst RAG-Systeme, um interne Wissensquellen (Produktdaten, Anleitungen, FAQ-Inhalte) für LLM-Anwendungen nutzbar zu machen – von der Datenstrukturierung über Vektordatenbanken bis zur robusten Pipeline.
Datenanalyse & Python-Pipelines: Du entwickelst Auswertungen auf Basis unserer Bestell- und Produktdaten z.B. Warenkorbanalysen oder Content-Quality-Scoring.
Interne Tools: Du erweiterst unsere interne Tool-Plattform (React/TypeScript/Express, Node.js) um neue Module und Dashboards für die Fachbereiche.
Infrastruktur: Unsere Systeme laufen self-hosted auf Linux-Servern (Docker Compose, Nginx). Du bringst deine Lösungen selbst in Produktion – Deployment gehört bei uns dazu.
Qualifikation
Ausbildung: Studium in Informatik, Data Science, Wirtschaftsinformatik o.ä. – oder gleichwertige Praxis als Quereinsteiger. Uns interessiert, was du gebaut hast, nicht nur, was auf dem Papier steht.
n8n / Automatisierung: Sehr gute Kenntnisse in n8n (oder Make/Zapier mit Wechselbereitschaft), inklusive Entwicklung, Fehlerbehandlung und Betrieb skalierbarer Workflows.
AI-Coding: Du entwickelst mit modernen AI-Coding-Tools wie Claude Code als festem Bestandteil deines Workflows – von der Idee über den Code bis zum Deployment. Ein Grundverständnis für Python oder JavaScript/TypeScript ist von Vorteil, aber kein Muss – wichtiger ist, dass du weißt, was du baust, und Ergebnisse kritisch prüfen kannst.
LLMs & KI: Fundierte Praxis mit LLM-APIs (z.B. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) und echtes Interesse an aktuellen Entwicklungen. Erfahrung mit RAG-Architekturen, Embeddings und Vektordatenbanken ist ein Plus, ebenso Erfahrung mit lokalen Modellen (Ollama).
Datenbanken: Sicherer Umgang mit SQL (MySQL/MariaDB, idealerweise auch MSSQL). Du kannst komplexe Abfragen über große Datenmengen schreiben und optimieren.

At Flix, we offer a dynamic work environment with competitive pay, strong growth opportunities, and a tech-driven approach to making travel more accessible, sustainable, and affordable. 

Flix is reshaping how customers get help, moving towards AI-driven resolution across every channel, language, and market. As a Process Automation Engineer (Celonis) (m/f/d) , you turn that ambition into running systems: you design and deliver end-to-end automated processes on the Celonis platform that resolve real customer cases without human intervention, for millions of passengers.

You bring engineering rigour into a business team. You translate business requirements into data models, pipelines, and automations fast, you own what you ship in production, and you are comfortable being the most technical person in the room.

· Data integration and modelling: identify the source-system tables and fields that need to be brought into Celonis ; build and maintain the extractions, transformations (ETL) and Celonis data models for each Customer Service process, spanning ticketing, order management, and payment/refund data.

· Automation development: design, build, and operate production automations on the Celonis platform (Action Flows and Process Orchestrator) that execute real customer outcomes (e.g. end-to-end refund handling), including API calls into Flix backend systems and integrations with AI-driven customer contact channels (chatbot, voicebot ).

· Reliability and guardrails: your automations move real money; build for scalability, error handling, monitoring, auditability, and safe rollout of changes.

· Insourcing and takeover: take over data models and automation logic built by an external implementation partner (reverse-engineer, document, harden, and extend them as the in-house owner).

· Collaboration: work daily with business users who own rules and business logic, the Data Analyst who owns dashboards and process mining, and IT engineering who own system integrations, security, and scalability.

· Documentation: document all technical and data requirements and all ETL and automation work to Centre of Excellence standards, so nothing you build depends on you being in the room.

· Automation platform experience: 3+ years hands-on building production automations on process orchestration or automation platforms; Celonis is a strong plus (Data Integration, PQL, Knowledge Models, Action Flows, Process Orchestrator); strong experience with platforms such as n8n, Camunda, UiPath, Power Automate, or Make is also relevant. We care about proven end-to-end delivery, not certifications.

· Production ownership at scale: you have owned and shipped solutions handling transactions at scale (1M+ annually) and can talk concretely about what broke and how you fixed it.

· Data fundamentals: working SQL and data modelling basics; you understand how to identify a correct case ID, control grain in joins, and validate a data model against its sources. Scripting (Python or similar) is a plus but not required (you are comfortable using AI tooling to fill gaps here).

· Enterprise systems and integration literacy: solid understanding of how core operational systems work — CRM, ticketing, order management, and ERP — including their data structures, process flows, and the business logic they enforce. Equally, you are fluent in how these systems integrate: REST and SOAP APIs, authentication mechanisms, webhooks, rate limits, and data exchange formats (JSON, XML). You can independently read API documentation, navigate integration patterns, and reason about data flow across system boundaries.

· Hybrid profile: you thrive in a roughly 70/30 technical-business role: you sit inside the business, gather requirements yourself, and can explain and defend technical decisions to non-technical stakeholders.

· Communication: clear written documentation and communication in English; you leave behind artefacts other people can pick up.

· Conversational automation experience: hands-on experience connecting automated workflows to chatbot or voicebot platforms is a plus.

We recognize that everyone carries a unique set of valuable skills and experiences. If you think you could have an impact even though you don't meet 100% of the requirements, we still encourage you to apply. We want to hear from you!

We are looking for a Senior Hardware Test Engineer to be a technical cornerstone of our Test Engineering pillar within the broader Product Reliability Function. Our collar is tough and built for the beating it takes day in and day out on a farm, but it can always be tougher.

We've iterated it to this point and learnt many tough lessons along the way. We need someone who can design and execute automated tests across 100's of samples, that turn assumptions into evidence; someone who brings rigour, creativity, and speed to every challenge they take on.
Our devices face demanding field conditions at incredible scale. We'll be the first virtual fencing company ever with 1 million devices live, and with some customers deploying thousands of units per herd, our testing must be comprehensive, automated and traceable back to product requirements on top of accounting for every edge case to guarantee reliability.
Hardware is only getting more important strategically for Halter, and you'll be right at the core, making that happen. It's a rare opportunity to accelerate your career with unique and valuable experience in a high-performance, fast-paced environment where product reliability matters most and test automation, repeatability and traceability are your tools.
This role reports to our Hardware Test Engineering Manager and sits within the Product Reliability Function. You'll be the person who owns the test strategy and test infrastructure, builds the tests, builds the rigs, analyses the data, and delivers the evidence that drives confident product decisions.
What you'll own
Your work produces the evidence that decides whether we ship, whether we hold, and what we fix next. You'll operate with a high degree of autonomy across test design, execution, and infrastructure.

s.h: Design, build, and run tests that matter
s.t:
Own and execute the test automation strategy and overarching infrastructure (likely in Python or Teststand)
Design and execute environmental, reliability, verification and validations tests across electromechanical sub-systems and full product assemblies: HALT, UV exposure, tumble, impact, thermal cycling, ingress, and more.
Own tests end-to-end: from interpreting product requirements and writing test plans through to execution, analysis, and delivering clear pass/fail evidence.
Identify gaps in requirements or test coverage and propose new methods or approaches to close them.

Design and build bespoke test rigs, fixtures, and automation that makes testing faster, more repeatable, more reproducible and less manual.
Own, maintain and integrate environmental chambers, DAQ systems, RF systems and other equipment into the test automation infrastructure, ensuring the infrastructure is always calibrated and up to a high standard.
Continuously raise the bar on test and data throughput without compromising evidential quality or repeatability.

Ensure every test produces data that is trustworthy, traceable, and actionable—not just raw numbers, but clear evidence that links back to requirements or risks that engineering leadership can rely on for go/no-go decisions.
Maintain strong test governance practices: calibration records, equipment versioning, code versioning, procedure versioning, and full traceability.
Present findings clearly to cross-functional stakeholders, turning complex results into crisp recommendations.

Partner closely with Reliability Engineering, Hardware Design, Firmware, and Production to ensure quality testing approaches are embedded early in the development cycle, not bolted on at the end.
Work with Reliability Engineers to translate reliability requirements and product requirements into robust, efficient and scaleable test plans.
Contribute to a culture of evidence over opinions —where "reliable" and "quality" means "proven," NOT "seems fine."
What success looks like
Tests you design and run are repeatable, well-documented, and trusted across the organisation.
Your evidence directly enables Halter to ship with confidence, driven by data rather than hope.
Test infrastructure you build scales with the team—others can pick up your rigs, procedures, and methods and run with them.
Reliability and Quality improves with every release, and your work is a key reason why.

You're a hands-on engineer who builds things that work
Significant experience in hardware test engineering or validation in high-reliability environments (IoT, ruggedised consumer electronics, automotive, aerospace, industrial, robotics, or similar).
You've designed and run environmental and reliability tests, and you understand the science behind the stress methods, not just the procedures.
You know the tools and the reality
Strong experience at building a scalable and automated test infrastructure
Strong experience with environmental testing, accelerated life testing, and reliability stress methods such as HALT/UV/Tumble/Impact etc.
Proven ability to design and build bespoke test jigs, fixtures, instrumentation, DAQ systems, and automation.
Solid calibration discipline and an instinct for where precision matters versus where "good enough" is actually good enough.
Comfortable with data analysis, automate reporting and able to draw clear conclusions and value from test results.
You operate with ownership and clarity
You take end-to-end ownership of your work and hold yourself to a high standard.
You communicate clearly—your test reports, presentations, and recommendations are easy to act on.
You thrive in cross-functional environments and collaborate with high standards and low ego.

We've spent the last two years rebuilding the platform from the ground up: new customer app, new Pro onboarding, job distribution engine, and data infrastructure. The foundation is solid. Now we're moving into expanded service verticals, dynamic pricing, and AI-powered features at scale. Quality needs to keep up.
Our stack is PHP (Laravel) and React/React Native, with Cypress as our primary test framework. We actively use Claude Code as part of our engineering workflow, not as an experiment, but as a core part of how we work.

As we scale into new service verticals and grow the engineering team, quality can't be reactive. This role exists to make quality proactive: owning the automation coverage, shaping the bug process, and partnering closely with Product, Design, and the Data team to catch problems before they reach customers.
You'll report to the Engineering Manager and be embedded across the engineering organization. This is hands-on and strategic, helping raise the quality ceiling for the whole team.

Cross-functional influence : You work directly with engineers, PMs, Designers, and the Data team to surface risks early, understand requirements deeply, and propose better solutions. You may be embedded in one or two delivery teams.
Automation ownership : You own the strategy for building and expanding our automated test coverage, not just executing test cases someone else wrote.
Process shaper : You'll identify gaps in our quality process and have the authority to fix them, not just flag them.
What You'll Own
Automated test coverage : Design and grow our E2E and integration test suite using Cypress. Set the strategy, prioritize coverage gaps, and raise the floor across the platform.
Bug process : Own the full lifecycle from triage to production fix. Keep it moving, keep stakeholders informed, and make sure nothing falls through the cracks.
Cross-functional quality partnership : Collaborate with PMs, Designers, and the Data team to review requirements, raise risks early, and define what "done" actually means.
Process improvement : Identify weaknesses in how we deliver software and propose solutions. Not just document them.
Exploratory testing : Test new features and existing flows on web and mobile across devices, catching what automation misses.
Problems to Solve
Keeping automation coverage sharp as the product evolves Our E2E coverage is solid. The challenge is staying ahead: bringing new ideas, exploring different types of coverage, and finding smarter ways to automate different aspects of the application as the product grows and new service verticals come online.
Exploring new tools and leveraging AI to improve quality operations AI is changing how we build software, and it's changing how we can test it too. There's real opportunity here to use AI tools to increase output quality, cut repetitive work, and discover coverage gaps we'd otherwise miss. We want someone who actively explores that space, not someone who waits to be told what to use.
What Success Looks Like (Year 1)
Automation coverage stays strong : New features ship with automated tests as a baseline, and coverage strategies evolve with the product.
Bug process runs smoothly : Triage to fix cycle is predictable and stakeholders know where things stand without having to ask.
Deep business knowledge : You understand how the marketplace works well enough to anticipate edge cases on your own.
Quality process improvement shipped : At least one meaningful improvement to how we deliver quality is in place and being used by the team.

AI-native. You use AI tools like Claude Code to write, maintain, and extend test code, not as a novelty, but as a standard part of how you work. You're comfortable with browser MCPs, agent workflows, and building scripts that automate the boring parts of QA. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI in the engineering workflow.
Automation-first. Your default when you find a problem is to ask how to prevent it automatically. You build test infrastructure that outlasts any individual test case. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your strength is manual testing and automation is something you tolerate rather than drive.
Customer-obsessed. You think like a user. When you're testing a flow, you're asking whether it actually works for a real customer, not just whether it matches the spec. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you treat quality as a checkbox rather than a standard.
Adaptable. You don't get attached to a single tool, stack, or process. We're in a period of rapid evolution in how software gets built and tested, especially with AI, and you lean into that rather than resist it. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you thrive only in stable, well-defined tooling environments.
Collaborative and direct. You work across Product, Design, Engineering, and Operations. You surface risks early, speak plainly about what you find, and push back when something isn't ready to ship. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you prefer to work in isolation or soften feedback to avoid friction.
Technically solid. You're comfortable reading and writing code. You understand front and backend web services well enough to test them properly, write meaningful SQL queries, and debug issues across the stack. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your technical depth is limited to a single layer or framework.
This Role Is NOT
A manual-testing role : Most of your testing work should be building automation, not executing test scripts by hand.
A ticket-executor role : You're expected to shape what gets worked on and how, not just process a backlog.
A single-tool role : We use Cypress today, but we adapt. If you're only comfortable in one framework or one part of the stack, this will be limiting.
A role for someone who avoids ambiguity : The business is changing fast. New verticals, new flows, new edge cases. You need to be comfortable moving before everything is defined.
A back-of-the-line role : Quality is a first-class concern here. You're expected to have opinions and influence the process upstream, not just verify what's already been built.

Equity: We want you invested in the quality and long-term health of the platform you're helping build.
Fully remote: Work from anywhere in the Americas. Deep focus and async collaboration are the norm here.
Unlimited PTO: We focus on results. Take what you need.
